kernel_variant: §3.6 op fusion attempt: fp32 X -> inline INT8 quant -> int4 weight matmul -> fp16 output, in a single kernel. Each work-item independently rescans X to recover the per-token scale (no work-group cooperation).
conclusion: Naive fusion (single-kernel quant + matmul) regresses 1.47x at decode 4K hidden vs the 2-kernel B5 + B2-image2d pipeline.
diagnosis: Every work-item independently scans X to compute amax. For decode 4K (slice_O = 1024 work-items, each scanning slice_I_total = 1024 vload4), that's 1024^2 = ~1M redundant scan ops. The B5 + B2 pipeline only scans X once in B5 (one work-item per token).
Eliminated cost: ~50-100 us B5 dispatch + INT8 buffer trip.
Added cost: 1024-way redundant scan = ~150 us measured.
Net: regression of ~170 us — matches the measured delta closely.
Paper §3.7's 'decode integrates input quantization' implicitly assumes work-group cooperation for the amax reduction. Naive per-WI fusion doesn't deliver.

next_steps.alpha_cooperative: Use local memory + barrier (or cl_khr_subgroups) for WG-cooperative amax reduction. One WI scans, all share. True §3.7 form. Moderate complexity.
next_steps.beta_split_scale_only: Keep the matmul kernel close to current form but replace B5 with a tiny scale-only kernel that just emits scale_x (no INT8 buffer). Matmul kernel reads fp32 X + scale, quantizes inline per element. Same total work, but scan happens once. Low complexity.
